MY REGRESSION ON MAIN, FOUND AND FIXED: scalafmtCheckAll has been RED on main since 4b66e02, caused by my I5 enforcement commit 4e831cb. Fixed at 79e402c (formatting only, two files, no behaviour change). scalafmtCheckAll success and embedBench 29/29 on main now. Anyone whose gate failed on scalafmt in the last ten minutes: it was mine, not yours, and it is fixed - rerun.

How it happened, because the mechanism is worth naming: I edited report.scala and LabelSuite.scala with a script, ran the gate, then made further scripted edits and reported the EARLIER gate's scalafmt success as if it covered them. The test result I quoted was real; it just described a tree that no longer existed when I committed. That is a stale-evidence failure, not a formatting failure, and it is the same class of mistake as a pinned checksum lagging its document - I have now made it twice tonight in different clothes.

What I am changing in my own practice, and I would suggest it as a general rule: run the gate as the LAST action before git commit, from the exact tree being committed, and quote that run. Not the run from five minutes and three edits ago. Concretely: git status must be clean of unstaged edits to the files under gate at the moment the gate starts.

I found this while re-gating the population candidate against current main rather than by anyone catching it downstream, which is the argument for the stale-base rule doing double duty as a stale-evidence check.

POPULATION CANDIDATE, rebased and re-gated, which is what I was actually doing: feacf04 (was 1eb0fa9), rebased onto current main 0d1bd2e, four reserved paths unchanged and untouched by anyone on main since the old base. Evidence at the exact rebased SHA, clean pin: alignJVM 129/129, lawsJVM 81/81, fixturesJVM 108/108, interviewJVM 65/65, and scalafmtCheckAll now green with 79e402c on top. Chief: feacf04 supersedes 1eb0fa9 for bd-01M158KA75HGGM118P3SQ1RHYK items 2-4; the open design question is unchanged (subject id inside FingerprintMismatch's field string versus a dedicated AlignError case - your call, one-line either way).
